name: Vanessa Biceps
tagline: Quiet strength has never had so much character.
story: Vanessa plays with a contrast that is impossible to forget: a delicate look and oversized arms. Her polka dot dress and gentle expression set an immediately identifiable tone, somewhere between situational humor and campaign presence. She works just as well in a very simple portrait as in an offbeat scene where her calm is the whole gag.
uses: A character for stories of daily life turned upside down, campaigns of quiet strength and social formats based on contrast.

name: Josiane Cornichon
tagline: It never goes unnoticed at the checkout.
story: Josiane transports the ordinary into an absurd universe: a face with pickle textures, a familiar work outfit and a look that already tells the story of an entire day. Its potential lies in this gap between a recognizable profession and an impossible silhouette.
uses: A world of imaginary commerce, racing scenes and little everyday comedies.

name: Mr. Eyes on Vacation
tagline: The spirit has already left, the costume remains.
story: A slightly tired suit, a briefcase and eyes that seem to look elsewhere: this character alone carries a little story of the office and escape. The close-ups make his expressions readable; the full-length views emphasize the comical fragility of his silhouette.
uses: A mascot of work stories, dream vacations and offbeat humor.

name: Miss Ears Parables
story: The brown bob, glasses and retro clothing give him immediate familiarity. His giant ears then change all the proportions and make a simple look into a real character expression. It naturally lends itself to stories of listening, curiosity and unexpected conversations.
uses: A character for stories of communication, curiosity and comedic reaction sequences.

name: Madame Permanente Volcan
story: Everything about her claims its place: monumental hair, golden accessories and a pink outfit that doesn't try to be discreet. Her tiny face amid the curls enhances her comic power. Each pose can become a mood statement.
uses: A mascot for assertive confidence, fashion diversions and diva characters.

name: Queen Front Panoramic
tagline: A very big sense of his own importance.
story: An oversized forehead and a heavily dressed figure create an instantly recognizable comedy queen. The pink outfit, jewelry and posture build a confident personality, while the expressions introduce the touch of absurdity that makes it memorable.
uses: A world of offbeat fashion, small fictional rivalries and reactions full of character.

name: Brigitte Bamboo
tagline: The head in the moon, the silhouette in the clouds.
story: Brigitte combines a very stretched silhouette with a round head and an almost silent beige palette. His apparent calm, raised eyes and economical gestures provide an observational humor different from the louder characters in the cast. She can bring a scene to life with very few props.
uses: A presence for dreamy stories, minimalist scenes and proportion gags.

name: Cindy Parpaing
story: Cindy brings together a very clean bob cut, a sports outfit in retro colors and a silhouette whose proportions tell the whole story. His somewhat detached expression contrasts with the exaggeration of the body, which allows him to play comedy without multiplying the gestures.
uses: A mascot for fictional streetwear, 90s hijinks and attitude humor.

name: Ginette Bulldozer
tagline: The flowers are delicate. Ginette, a little less.
story: Ginette contrasts the softness of a floral dress with a strong natural build. The red curls, the glasses and the little upset expression give a very precise character anchor. She can be funny while remaining still: the contrast is enough to establish the situation.
uses: A protagonist for stories of determination, neighborhood scenes and ordinary situations turned upside down.

name: Monica Turbo
story: Monique enters the frame with the energy of a race already underway. Yellow, pink and sporty glasses give a strong chromatic identity, while the jaw and expressions tip the portrait into an assumed caricature.
uses: A mascot of energy and challenge for sporting stories and offbeat campaigns.

name: Count Shoulders Hanger
tagline: He is always a shoulder length ahead.
story: Her patterned purple suit and her monumental shoulders depict a theatrical nobility, too sure of herself to be entirely serious. The small head, the mustache and the raised chin make the variations of expression particularly readable.
uses: A character for parodic prestige stories, baroque universes and emphatic speeches.

name: Lady Neck Accordion
story: Pearls, gloves and a light jacket establish an elegant vocabulary that the tiered neck immediately diverts. Its profile gives a strong graphic sign; close-ups and seated poses help develop a haughty and comical personality.
uses: A mascot for satirical fashion, salon stories and theatrical reactions.

name: Lady Sauerkraut
tagline: An authority that takes up all the space.
story: A flamboyant bun, severe glasses and a silhouette in a mustard suit: Dame Choucroute transforms the slightest glance into a comedy verdict. His exaggerated proportions make his face the center of every scene.
uses: Office scenes, reactions of disapproval and character portraits.

name: Jean Philargent
tagline: The smile is big. The jaw too.
story: Jean Philargent cultivates an elegance that is too confident to go unnoticed: double-breasted jacket, thin glasses and spectacular smile. His square jaw and confident gestures give his performances an immediately recognizable presence.
uses: A character for prestige hijinks, grandiose announcements and imaginary success stories.

name: Mr Pigeon
tagline: Lots of panache. A sense of charm all his own.
story: Monsieur Pigeon combines the look of a retro seducer with a neck of iridescent feathers and a beak that is impossible to ignore. His leopard shirt, his shiny jacket and his expressions create an urban universe full of mischief.
uses: Dating comedies, offbeat reactions and light-hearted street stories.
